## loco/

Our own runtime layer, outside the generated section above: the Locomotive text layer
(`txt.asm`, `print.asm`, `number.asm`, `screen.asm`, `inkey.asm`), licensed under MIT like the
rest of `lib/`. These files are written for this project and are not imported; the importer
leaves them alone. See `loco/README.md`.

## Firmware maths: the private-block slots (FWM-CORE)

In firmware builds REAL `+ - * /`, `^`, SQR, EXP, LOG, LOG10, SIN, COS, TAN, ATN, RND, the digits of the number text
(PREP), VAL's `x 10^E` and ROUND call the CPC firmware's maths pack through the gate (`loco/fwmath.asm`, over
`runtime/fwcall.asm`). The pack reads its operands with the lower ROM enabled, so they are never passed from where the
program lives (below &4000): they sit in the private runtime block (`CPC_PRIV_BASE`, &9E00 in firmware mode), in bytes the
imported `sysvars.asm` leaves free (&F3-&FF; `loco/fwmath.asm` defines the names):

| Offset | Size | Name | Content |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| &F3 | 5 | `FWM_A` | the first operand and the result (HL on entry to the firmware entry) |
| &F8 | 5 | `FWM_B` | the second operand (DE on entry) |
| &FD | 2 | `FWM_TBL` | the entry table of this machine (0 until the first maths call detects it with `KL PROBE ROM`: H = 0 for the 464, 1 for the 664, 2 for the 6128, 4 for the 6128 Plus; three tables, 464 / 664 / 6128 and Plus) |

The gate saves and restores IX and IY (every entry corrupts them), treats BC, DE and AF as lost, takes the carry as the success
flag, and needs 64 bytes of stack (40 measured). The slots and the gate are not re-entrant: the interrupt handler never calls
the maths. Bare builds have no firmware and keep the imported calculator behind the same `__LOCO_F*` entries. The entry
addresses, the register contract and the error protocol are in the header of `loco/fwmath.asm`.

### REAL speed and size

Because firmware builds use the firmware's maths, results match Locomotive bit for bit and `+ - * /`, `^` and the
functions are faster than the interpreter. On an emulated 6128 `a+b` takes 0.59 ms against 0.93 ms, `SIN(a)` 13.59 ms
against 13.72 ms, and the whole float benchmark 8.98 s against Locomotive's 9.57 s. A bare build uses the software
calculator (8 significant digits, its own `RND`, a Newton-method `SQR`): `SQR(a)` takes 21.46 ms (the firmware's takes
26.56 ms), but `SIN(a)` takes 40.98 ms and the benchmark 14.36 s. `STR$`, `VAL`, `INT`, `RND` and comparisons of REALs
are currently slower than the interpreter (`STR$` 11.03 ms against 5.95 ms, `VAL` 8.70 ms against 3.65 ms); an improvement
is planned. Programs are on the whole smaller than the frozen Boriel fork's (382 896 bytes against 445 527 over 41 programs,
14.1 % smaller), except REAL-heavy ones (`floats`: 9 741 bytes against 7 497). Prefer `INTEGER` or `FIXED` in game loops.
The figures were measured on CPCEC timings of emulated machines.

## Files and the AMSDOS buffers (L4-FILES)

Files are firmware only (`loco/filecom.asm`, `file.asm`, `fileout.asm`, `write.asm`: AMSDOS through the CAS entries; a bare build
refuses the statements with E270). AMSDOS wants a 2 KB buffer for each stream that is open, which the program gives it
directly under the private block, so the memory map of a firmware build is, from the top:

| Range | Content |
| --- | --- |
| &A200-&A5FF (stack, top &A600) | the stack; CHAIN copies its loader to &A200 |
| &9E00-&A1FF | the private runtime block |
| &9600-&9DFF | the input stream's buffer (OPENIN, LOAD, CAT, CHAIN), present when the program uses any of them |
| &8E00-&95FF | the output stream's buffer (OPENOUT, PRINT #9, WRITE #9, SAVE) when the input stream's is present too; with the output stream alone it takes &9600-&9DFF |
| below | the heap (top-aligned under the buffers when `--heap-address` is not given), then the program from its origin |

A program that never opens a file loses nothing: the buffers exist only when `loco/file.asm` or `loco/fileout.asm` is linked
(`PRINT #9` on its own, which is error 31 at run time, needs neither). `codegen/memory-map.ts` has the numbers
(`FILE_BUFFER_SIZE`, `fileBufferBytes`); `makeTarget` lowers the default heap by them and defines `__LOCO_FILE_IN` for
`fileout.asm`; the layout check gives E405 for code or data that ends inside the buffers and E406 for a heap that overlaps
them. The runtime starts AMSDOS before its first file call (`KL INIT BACK` with the boot's limits, `&A67C-&B0FF`, because a program
started by `RUN"` has the disc ROM shut down), keeps a file name on the stack in capitals (AMSDOS wants it in the central 32 KB),
and records AMSDOS's error code (bit 7 set) in the slot DERR reads. `CHAIN "name"` loads another binary over the running one: it
checks that the file opens, puts the firmware's interrupt vector back at &0038, copies a loader above the private block and calls
MC BOOT PROGRAM, which stops the timers and the sound and starts the new program as `RUN"` does.

## Known defects in `runtime/`

The imported files stay byte copies of the fork, so defects found in them are listed here
until a task fixes them (we maintain the runtime now; a fix changes the file and this list
together, and the asm golden programs that link the file are re-checked).

Fixed here and patched by `tools/import-runtime.py` (`PATCHED`, so `--check` accepts them):
`arith/div8.asm` line 60, `xor l` to `xor e` (the sign of a signed 8-bit division). The six
`tests/asm-golden/runtime/` `.bin` files that include it carry the changed byte (0xAD to 0xAB);
the program fixtures keep the fork's text and bytes.
`fp_calc.asm`, SKIP-CONS (`L33F7`): `ld de, 0` became `ld de, FP_CALC_STACK_END - 5` (follow-up 43). The
Spectrum ROM calls STK-CONST there with DE = 0, a write into ROM that is ignored; on the CPC the lower
ROM is paged out, so every series evaluation (SQR, SIN, COS, TAN, ATN, LN, EXP, powers) zeroed
`&0000-&0004`, the firmware's RST 0 routine. The 68 `tests/asm-golden/runtime/` and `library/` `.bin`
files that link it carry the changed operand (2 bytes each: `&9E7D` firmware, `&BC7D` bare).
`mem/alloc.asm`, `__MEM_LOOP`: the failure path under `#ifdef __MEMORY_CHECK__` loads error 7 (Locomotive's
Memory full) instead of `ERROR_OutOfMemory` (the Spectrum's 3). cpcbas defines `__MEMORY_CHECK__` in every
build (`codegen/target.ts`), so a string that cannot be allocated stops with `Error 7` instead of carrying on
with an empty string (follow-up 50). No golden wrapper defines it, so no fixture changes.
`error.asm` (L4-ERR, docs/ir.md "Errors"): the `ERROR_*` values are Locomotive's error numbers (SubscriptWrong 9, OutOfMemory 7, OutOfScreen 5,
NumberTooBig 6, InvalidArg 5, IntOutOfRange 5, NonsenseInBasic 2, InvalidColour 5; follow-up 21), and `__ERROR` jumps to the ON ERROR trap (the
word `LOCO_ERRTRAP`, `SYSVAR_BASE + $220`, `loco/vars.asm`) when it is set, before it prints `Error n`; `__ERROR_FATAL` is the message path
(entry A = the number). `tools/import-runtime.py` holds the patch as a list of (old, new) pairs. Every program that links `error.asm` (all of them)
is 10 bytes (firmware) or 8 bytes (bare) longer. The reference assembler and compiler find the patched files of this list through an override directory
(`CPCBAS_OVERRIDE`, `tools/asm-oracle/driver.py` and `zxbc-driver.py`), so the golden fixtures that link a patched file are made from the patched source,
which also reproduces the hand-corrected `div8.asm` and `fp_calc.asm` fixtures exactly.
`txtglyph.asm` (L4-FIX, follow-up 130): the bare block graphics 128-143 are built in the CPC layout (bit 0 top left, bit 1 top right, bit 2
bottom left, bit 3 bottom right; the fork numbers them as the Spectrum), a three-part patch (two comments and the quadrant table `__CT_TQTAB`).
The 15 `tests/asm-golden/runtime/` bare `.bin` files that link it, and the two bare program fixtures, carry the changed table.

- `val.asm`, `VAL`: for a NULL string (`VAL_EMPTY`) and for a string of length 0 (`VAL_DONE`
  before the accumulator is pushed) it ends with `__FPSTACK_POP` without having pushed
  anything, so it returns whatever lies below the floating-point stack and leaves the stack
  one entry short. The compiler never calls it directly: `VAL` is `__LOCO_VAL`
  (`loco/strval.asm`), which skips blanks and a `+` and passes the text `"0"` when nothing is
  left, so `VAL` only ever sees a non-empty string.
- `arith/divf16.asm`, `__DIVF16`: the header comment ("DE.HL = Dividend, Stack Top = Divisor")
  is the reverse of what the code does. The CALLEE entry moves the stacked value into the
  working register set as the dividend, so the quotient is `stack / DEHL`. The code is right
  and the compiler relies on it (`packages/cpcbas/src/codegen/real.ts`, `tDivF16`, pushes the
  first operand); `test/real-run.test.ts` pins `a / b` both ways. Only the comment is wrong.

## The BASIC library (`cpcbuild.bas`, `cpcbuild/`, `cpcplus/`, `music/`, `stdlib/`)

Ported from CPCBuild's `lib/` (MIT, same author; commit `54e3580` of that repository, 2026-11-08) and
from the CPC stdlib of the fork of Boriel BASIC 1.19 (`src/lib/arch/cpc/stdlib`, `cpc.bas` and
`framehook.bas`; Boriel BASIC is by José Manuel Rodríguez de la Rosa and contributors, MIT for the
library). CPCBuild keeps its own frozen copy until it switches to this one. The licence of everything
here is `LICENSE` (MIT); the Arkos Tracker 3 player `music/akg_cpc.asm` is MIT too
(Copyright (c) 2016-2025 Julien Nevo; `music/LICENSE.arkos`). `#include <cpcbuild.bas>` (or any one
file, `#include <music/music.bas>`, `#include <cpc.bas>`) finds the file in this tree after the
program's own directory and the `-I` paths; `stdlib/` is searched as well, so `cpc.bas` and
`framehook.bas` need no prefix.

### Quick start

Include the whole game library with one line, or one part of it. Only the SUBs and FUNCTIONs
the program calls are meant to cost memory (see "Unused procedures" below).

```basic
#include <cpcbuild.bas>

DIM ball(7) AS UBYTE => {&3C, &7E, &FF, &FF, &FF, &FF, &7E, &3C}
DIM x AS INTEGER = 38

MODE 1
ScreenInit()
DO
    ScanKeys()
    IF KeyDown(KEY_RIGHT) THEN x = x + 1
    IF KeyDown(KEY_LEFT) THEN x = x - 1
    WaitRetrace(1)
    ClearScreen(0)
    PutSprite(x, 96, 1, 8, @ball)
LOOP
```

This builds with `-D CPC464`, `-D CPC6128` and `-D PLUS`, and with `-D CPC_BAREMETAL`. Coordinates
in `cpcbuild/` are x in screen bytes (0 to 79) and y in pixel lines (0 to 199), from the top left.
`@ball` is the address of the first element of the array. Each file's header comment (at the top
of the `.bas` file) is its full reference.

### What each file offers

| Include | Procedures |
|---|---|
| `cpcbuild.bas` | includes `cpcbuild/display.bas`, `sprites.bas`, `fill.bas`, `tiles.bas`, `keyboard.bas`, `palette.bas`, `spritelist.bas` and `text.bas`; `banks.bas` is not part of it (`#include <cpcbuild/banks.bas>`) |
| `cpcbuild/display.bas` | `ScreenInit`, `WaitRetrace`, `EnableDoubleBuffer`, `DisableDoubleBuffer`, `FlipBuffer`, `PokeScreen`, `PeekScreen` |
| `cpcbuild/sprites.bas` | `PutSprite`, `PutSpriteMasked`, `GetBlock` |
| `cpcbuild/spritelist.bas` | `SprListBegin`, `SprListDraw`, `SprListEnd`, `SprListReset`, `SprListPaper` |
| `cpcbuild/fill.bas` | `PenByte`, `FillRect`, `ClearScreen` |
| `cpcbuild/tiles.bas` | `SetTileSet`, `SetTileWidth`, `TileWidth`, `DoTile8`, `DoTile16`, `TileMap`, `TileMapPart`, `TileRestore` |
| `cpcbuild/text.bas` | `TextFont`, `TextPen`, `TextAt`, `TextAtBoth`, `TextFlush` |
| `cpcbuild/keyboard.bas` | `ScanKeys`, `KeyDown`, `AnyKeyDown`, and the `KEY_` and `JOY_` constants |
| `cpcbuild/palette.bas` | `SetPalette`, `PalUpload` |
| `cpcbuild/banks.bas` | `BankAvailable`, `BankSelect`, `BankOff`, `BankSelected`, `BankPeek`, `BankPoke`, `BankCopyIn`, `BankCopyOut`, `BankLoad` (`BankLoad` is not defined with `-D CPC_BAREMETAL`) |
| `cpcplus/cpcplus.bas` | the Plus hardware: `PlusAvailable`, `PlusUnlock`, `PlusLock`, `PlusPageIn`, `PlusPageOut`, `SetPalette12`, `SetBorder12`, `GetPalette12`, `SetPalette12Block`, `SpritePalette`, `SpriteColour`, `SpriteSetImage`, `SpriteSetImagePacked`, `SpriteMove`, `SpriteMoveBlock`, `SpriteMag`, `SpriteHide`, `SpritesHideAll`, `PlusPeek`, `PlusPoke`, `PlusPokeBlock`, `ScrollFine`, `ScrollBorder`, `SplitScreen`, `SplitScreenCrtc`, `SplitOff`, `RasterIntAt`, `RasterIntOff`, `RasterIntMove`, `RasterIntClear`, `DmaPrescaler`, `DmaStart`, `DmaStop`, `DmaAlign`, `DmaActive` (the `RasterInt` ones are not defined in firmware mode) |
| `cpcplus/palcycle.bas` | `PalCycleSet`, `PalCycleDir`, `PalCycleStop`, `PalCycleStep` |
| `cpcplus/sprman.bas` | `SprMgrInit`, `SprAlloc`, `SprAllocPacked`, `SprFree`, `SprSetImage`, `SprSetImagePacked`, `SprMove`, `SprMag`, `SprFlush`, `SprPending`, `SprUploads` |
| `music/music.bas` | the Arkos Tracker 3 player: `MusicInit`, `MusicHookUp`, `MusicInitBank`, `MusicFrame`, `MusicStop`, `SfxInit`, `SfxPlay`, `SfxStop` |
| `stdlib/cpc.bas` | `GetMode`, `SetInk`, `SetBorder`, `AyWrite`, `AyRead`, `SoundStop`, and in firmware mode `SoundQueue`, `SoundFree`, `SoundBusy`, `SoundEnvelope` |
| `stdlib/framehook.bas` | `FrameHook`, `FrameHookOff`, `Frames`, `GameMode` |

`cpcbuild/reserve.bas` holds one SUB, `CbReserve4000`, which marks &4000-&7FFF as reserved; the
double-buffer and bank procedures call it, and you do not call it yourself.

### Unused procedures

A SUB or FUNCTION that nothing reaches is not compiled. A procedure counts as reached when the main
program or a reached procedure calls it, takes its address with `@name`, or names its label in an
ASM block. Procedures of files included with `#include <...>` are dropped without a message, so
including all of `cpcbuild.bas` costs only what the program calls. Procedures of your own files
that nothing calls get warning W306.

### Procedures and RETURN

Inside a SUB or FUNCTION a bare `RETURN` returns from a `GOSUB` of that procedure (compile error E251 if the
procedure has no GOSUB). To leave early, use `EXIT SUB` or `EXIT FUNCTION`.

### Statements and the library

The Locomotive statements the compiler now has and the library's procedures overlap. The library works in
bare-metal builds, where the firmware statements are refused with error E270 (see the "Bare-metal builds" section of
[`../README.md`](../README.md)).

| Statement (needs the firmware) | Library procedures that work in both builds |
|---|---|
| `SOUND`, `ENV`, `ENT`, `RELEASE`, `SQ` | `MusicInit`, `MusicStop`, `SfxInit`, `SfxPlay`, `SfxStop` (`music/music.bas`); `AyWrite`, `AyRead`, `SoundStop` (`stdlib/cpc.bas`). `SoundQueue`, `SoundFree`, `SoundBusy` and `SoundEnvelope` are firmware only, like the statements. `BEEP` works in both |
| `INK n, c1, c2` flashing, `SPEED INK` | `SetInk`, `SetBorder`, `SetPalette` (the statement `INK` shows its first colour only in a bare build) |
| windows, `TAG`, `PRINT #s` | `TextFont`, `TextPen`, `TextAt` (`cpcbuild/text.bas`) |
| `KEY`, `KEY DEF`, `SPEED KEY` | `ScanKeys`, `KeyDown`, `AnyKeyDown` (`cpcbuild/keyboard.bas`) |

`FRAME`, `INKEY(n)`, `JOY(n)`, `PLOT`, `INK`, `ZONE`, `SYMBOL`, `PRINT USING`, `EVERY` and `AFTER` compile in both builds and
need no library. `FrameHook` (`stdlib/framehook.bas`) runs a machine-code routine once every frame, at the flyback, in both builds,
which a music player needs and a BASIC `EVERY` handler cannot promise.

`MC WAIT FLYBACK` (`CALL &BD19`, and `WaitVsync` that maps to it) waits for the flyback to be *on*, not for a new one: its loop
is `in a,(c) / rra / jr nc`, so called while a flyback is already in progress it returns at once. Ten of them in a row can take 3
frames in game mode, where the interrupt that would use up the pulse is the short game one. The `WaitRetrace` helper
of `tests/conformance/lib/fhlib.bas` lets a flyback in progress end first and is exact; use that pattern when you count frames.

### Files

Every `.asm` file under `cpcbuild/`, `cpcplus/` and `music/` is copied byte for byte (and assembles
byte-identically to the reference assembler: `tests/asm-golden/library`). The `.bas` files are
translated by the table of the language specification (Boriel to CPC BASIC): `BAND` is `AND`, `$FF`
outside an ASM block is `&FF`, and `#pragma push/pop(case_insensitive)` is removed (CPC BASIC is case
insensitive). Truth values the API documents (`KeyDown`, `SprPending`... return 0 or 1) are unchanged.

| Path | What | Origin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cpcbuild.bas` | the umbrella include | CPCBuild |
| `cpcbuild/*.bas`, `cpcbuild/*.asm` | display, sprites, fill, tiles, keyboard, palette, sprite list, text, banks, reserve | CPCBuild |
| `cpcplus/*.bas`, `cpcplus/*.asm` | Plus hardware sprites, DMA, split screen, raster interrupts, palette cycling, sprite manager | CPCBuild |
| `music/music.bas`, `music/music_cpc.bas`, `music/quiet.bas`, `music/akg_cpc.asm`, `music/LICENSE.arkos` | the Arkos Tracker 3 player and a silent test song | CPCBuild (Arkos Tracker 3, MIT) |
| `stdlib/cpc.bas`, `stdlib/framehook.bas` | `SetInk`, `SetBorder`, `GetMode`, `AyRead`, `AyWrite`, the sound-queue wrappers; `FrameHook`, `Frames`, `GameMode` | fork of Boriel BASIC 1.19 (cpc stdlib) |

### Not ported

- `zxbuild/` (`sprites.asm`, `sprites.bas`), `music/music_zx.bas`, `music/akg_zx.asm`: Spectrum only.
- The rest of the fork's stdlib (`attr`, `font`, `input`, `keys`, `play`, `point`, `print42`,
  `print64`, `screen`, `sinclair`): Spectrum screen idioms that CPC BASIC has as statements, or nothing
  the library and the conformance programs use. `music/quiet.vt2` (a Vortex Tracker source) is not needed.

### Removals and renames

The L6 translator maps these.

| Boriel library | CPC BASIC | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Mode n` (`stdlib/cpc.bas`) | the statement `MODE n` | reserved word; the statement does the same job |
| `WaitVsync` | `FRAME`, or `CALL MC_WAIT_FLYBACK` (&BD19) | the same |
| parameter `pen` of `PenByte`, `FillRect`, `ClearScreen`, `SetPalette12`, `SetInk` | `penNo` | `PEN` is reserved (calls are positional, so no caller changes) |
| parameter `key` of `KeyDown` | `keyNo` | `KEY` is reserved |
| parameter `line` of `SplitScreen`, `SplitScreenCrtc`, `RasterIntAt`, `RasterIntOff` | `scanLine` | `LINE` is reserved |

`GetMode` is kept (there is no function for it).

### Other changes from CPCBuild's copy

- A SUB that cannot work in a build mode keeps its refusal stub, as in CPCBuild: only a *call* fails, with
  error E520 naming the missing label (for example `SoundQueue_needs_the_firmware__not_available_with_CPC_BAREMETAL`).
  In bare-metal mode (`-D CPC_BAREMETAL`): `SoundQueue`, `SoundFree`, `SoundBusy`, `SoundEnvelope`
  (`stdlib/cpc.bas`) and `BankLoad` (`cpcbuild/banks.bas`); in firmware mode: `RasterIntAt`, `RasterIntOff`,
  `RasterIntMove` and `RasterIntClear` (`cpcplus/cpcplus.bas`).
- `music/music_cpc.bas` requires `music/akg_cpc.asm` (`#require`) instead of `#include`-ing it inside an ASM
  block (the player is assembled with the runtime; the glue is still jumped over at program start). An
  `#include` inside an ASM block works too: the file's lines become lines of the block. `music/music.bas` includes `music_cpc.bas` directly (no architecture switch).
- `stdlib/cpc.bas` lost the Spectrum-colour remark of its header together with `Mode` and `WaitVsync`.

### Tests

`packages/cpcbas/test/library-compile.test.ts` builds a program that includes each `.bas` file and calls every
SUB and FUNCTION in it (read from the file), for `-D CPC464`, `-D CPC6128` and `-D PLUS`, in firmware mode and
with `-D CPC_BAREMETAL`. `tests/e2e/lib-smoke.bas` runs the library on an emulated CPC.
